description.narrative: The development objective of the Safety Net Project for Niger is to establish and support an effective safety net system which will increase access of poor and food insecure people to cash transfer and cash for work programs. There are four components to the project. The first component of the project is safety net system. This component will support the establishment of a well-performing safety net system by investing in management systems, targeting and payments systems, monitoring and evaluation and capacity building. The second component of the project is cash transfers for food security. The cash transfers and accompanying measures are expected to support poor and food insecure households by increasing their income and investing in their human capital. Subcomponent 2.1 will pay the first 10,000 beneficiaries, subcomponent 2.2 the remaining 70,000. The third component of the project is cash for work. Through short term labor intensive public works, this component will provide income support to 60,000 individuals in areas affected by temporary food insecurity to produce and maintain public goods. The fourth component of the project is project management. This component will finance costs related to the management of the project (including salaries, setting up the offices, and other recurrent costs), and acquiring physical assets.

The project development objective is to establish and support an effective and adaptive safety net system that will increase access of poor and vulnerable people to cash transfer and cash for work programs.

comment.narrative: <p>The project exceeded both the original and revised targets. The reduction of the revised target did not represent a reduction ofscope of the revised PDO, but rather a recalculation taking into account that households could have more than one member participating in CFW activities and that a smaller household size (6 instead of 7,7) was used. Project coverage actually increased, with 16,500 new cash transfer households in 3 new regions plus 5,000 households receiving shock-response cash.</p>

<p>The household targeting evaluation found that 83 per cent of the targeted households were chronically poor, which exceeded the revised target (70 per cent), as well as the original one (80 per cent).</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of villages receiving payments based on the frequency specified in the implementation manual
Households with access to the cash transfer system established by the Project
Days of temporary employment (broken down by gender)

comment.narrative: <p>The project generated a total of 3,379,000 days of temporary work, remaining at 94 per cent of the target. The shortfall in the number of days of temporary work generated was due, among other reasons, to absences that could not be recovered and insufficient number of workers in some villages. Also the fact that the CFW component did not reach the target of providing 50 per cent of days of temporary employment to women contributed to the shortfall.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiary households that have been identified and registered to receive monthly transfers for a 24-month period
Households participating in the accompanying measures (participation rate)

comment.narrative: <p>The shortfall in the number of households participating in the accompanying measures (87,331 against a target of 107,100) was due to a miscalculation linked to the design of the impact evaluation. When setting the end target, it was not considered that a cohort of beneficiaries would receive only cash).</p>

title.narrative: Registered families who are receiving the transfers

comment.narrative: <p>The achievement of the indicator remained above the end target of 95 percent. The actual achieved at completion is 97.2 percent because 4,182 beneficiary households in Diffa and Tahoua had not yet received all payments regularly by the project.</p>

title.narrative: Project management expenses ratio is inferior or equal to 10%

comment.narrative: <p>The project management expenses ratio is defined as ratio between operating expenses and total annual expenditures (initial expenses investments, operating and other recurrent costs.</p>

title.narrative: The impact evaluation is generating lessons

comment.narrative: <p>Six different evaluations were carried out in the timeframe of the project, generating important insights and learning.</p>

title.narrative: A management information system is developed
Households with access to the cash for work programs

comment.narrative: <p>The achieved target exceeds by large the revised target of 30,000. Originally, the project was targeted at 60,000 individuals but the PDO revision changed this approach to take into account the decision that up to two members of a single household could be identified and registered to work.</p>

title.narrative: Cash for work and DRF cash transfer beneficiaries in departments identified as vulnerable by the DN

comment.narrative: <p>Coordination with DNPGCA, particularly its EWS unit, allows for DRF and CFW activities to be 100 percent targeted to departments that DNPGCA had classified as vulnerable.</p>

title.narrative: Micro-projects that are functional at the end of each calendar year

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator exceeded the target as all the micro-project were found to be functional at end calendar year.</p>

title.narrative: Households receiving scaled up cash transfer assistance through the disaster risk financing mechanism

comment.narrative: <p>The actual achievement represents 94 per cent of the expected target. The slight shortfall was due to the fact that some eligible households were missed during registration in Diffa. Due to the emergency nature of the response to was not possible to reach out these beneficiaries at a second stage</p>

<p>Considerable progress has been made towards the establishment of a unified social registry. In fact two milestones (sub-indicators) out of three were achieved. However, the yes/no nature of the indicator does not allow for grasping this progress. Therefore theachievement of the indicator can be better reflected in the sum of the scores attributed to the three sub-indicators against their target (5 out of 6).</p>

title.narrative: Effectiveness of national SP systems to address Climate Adaptation and Disaster Risk Management

comment.narrative: <p>Composite indicator with rating from 1 to 6. The revised PAD (2016) set the end target at 4, corresponding to “the Government has an overall strategy for ASP and a set of programs which aim to improve resilience through clear links to CCA and DRM. The project has scored 3 out of 4 meaning “the government has a clearly formulated strategy on how to create CCA and DRM links with the SP system and may have begun implementing such links”.  To be noted that the ISRs refer to an end target of 6, which is the full achievement of the composite indicator, not the end target, as established by the revised PAD.</p>

title.narrative: Capacity of Nigers social protection systems to implement adaptive social protection programs

comment.narrative: <p>Composite indicator with ratings from 1 to 6 based on the implementation of the following systems: (i) Dedicated institutions and staff; (ii) Targeting, (iii) MIS; (iv) payment; (v) grievance mechanisms; (vi) monitoring and evaluation. The revised PAD (2016) set the end target at 5, but the project exceeded the target and was able to setup all the system (rate 6). To be noted that the ISRs erroneously refers to an end target of 6.</p>

title.narrative: The monitoring and evaluation mechanism of the DNPGCCA is fully operational and processing the data of all the units of the DNPGCCA.
